Consider the following statements:
I. In the finals of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju became the world's youngest winner after defeating the Russian player Ian Nepomniachtchi.
II. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record of becoming world's youngest ever Grandmaster.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 45th Chess Olympiad 2024 was a team competition held in Budapest (Hungary) from 10–23 September 2024. The Olympiad is a Swiss-system team tournament; unlike a knockout format, there is no separate “final match” played between two players. Therefore, Statement I is factually incorrect. The team of Gukesh D., Praggnanandhaa R. Arjun Erigaisi, Vidit Gujrathi and Harikrishna Pentala, with Srinath Narayanan as the captain. Gukesh Played phenomenal scoring 9 points in 10 games, earning individual gold medal on the top board. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player (born in 2009), achieved his third and final GM norm in Budapest, Hungary, on 30 June 2021 and, after surpassing the required rating threshold, met all the requirements for the FIDE Grandmaster title. At that time, he was 12 years, 4 months, and 25 days old. With this, he broke the 19-year-old record of Russian Sergey Karjakin (12 years 7 months) and became the youngest Grandmaster in chess history. Thus, Statement II is factually correct.

s: Double fault is the term used in which of the following sports?
x: A double fault is a tennis term: a server who faults on both serves loses the point. It is not used in football, badminton or golf.

s:
Which of the following statements with regard to the Grand Slam Tennis Tournaments is/are correct?
1. The tournaments have a shared governance structure establishing the partnership among the four Grand Slam tournaments.
2. They are open for entry to all internationally ranked tennis players above the age of 14.
3. There is a limitation on the number of 'Wild Cards' a player may receive to compete in a Grand Slam Tournament. Select the answer using the code given below:
x: Statement 1 is correct: The Grand Slam Rules make it clear that Grand Slam Tennis (GST) operates under a shared governance framework jointly managed by the four Grand Slam tournaments. Statement 2 is correct: The four Grand Slam Tournaments are open for entry to all internationally ranked tennis players with a ranking of 500 or better based on merit and without discrimination, subject only to the conditions herein set forth and to those provisions of the WTA Age Eligibility Rule adopted by the Grand Slam Tournaments and provided, however, that minors under the age of fourteen (14) shall not be eligible for entry. For purposes of this Rule, the player's age as of the first day of the tournament's Main Draw shall be used. • Note: Statement 2 appears to be incorrect based on the Grand Slam Rules, which state that all internationally ranked tennis players with a ranking of 500 or better are eligible to enter Grand Slam tournaments. However, as per the UPSC Provisional Answer Key, the correct answer has been given as "1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is incorrect: No rule limits the number of wild cards an individual player may receive across Grand Slam tournaments. Wild cards are given at each organiser's discretion. • Note: It is neither practical nor necessary for an aspirant to know every such highly specific, obscure information. We recommend aspirants avoid unnecessary guesswork in such highly factual questions.

s: Who was the winner of the men's singles at the 2015 Wimbledon Championships?
x: At the 2015 Wimbledon Championship, the men's singles title was won by Serbia's Novak Djokovic defeating Roger Federer of Switzerland. The winner of the 2025 Men's Singles was Jannik Sinner (Italy) and the runner-up was Carlos Alcaraz (Spain).

s: Viswanathan Anand won the FIDE World Chess Championship by defeating:
x: Veselin Topalov Viswanathan Anand defended his FIDE World Chess Championship title in 2010 by defeating Bulgarian grandmaster Veselin Topalov in a closely contested match held in Sofia, Bulgaria. This victory reaffirmed Anand's status as one of the greatest chess players of his era. He remained World 187 APPSC PYQS " Champion until losing the title to Magnus Carlsen in 2013.
